Scott Olson | Getty Images Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the company said it saw strength among professional shoppers. The company said comparable sales grew 1.8% for the quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales. Net sales grew to $22.76 billion. Because of the strength, Lowe's now said it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion. It also expects comparable sales to be up 0.5%, compared to previous guidance of flat. CEO Marvin Ellison told CNBC's Becky Quick on Wednesday that the company "can grow" despite economic headwinds and a sluggish housing market. In a separate statement, Ellison said the company posted its sixth straight quarter of comparable sales growth. Lowe's also reported a pre-tax benefit of approximately $250 million from tariff refunds during the quarter, which contributed a 34-cent boost to earnings per share. Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.10 adjusted, it was not immediately clear if that compared to the $2.88 expected Revenue: $22.76 billion vs. $22.41 billion expected For the quarter ended Oct. 31, Lowe's reported net income of $1.67 billion, or $2.98 per share, compared to $1.62 billion, or $2.88 per share, the year prior. The home improvement retailer has previously said it's seeing "pressure" on spending on projects, especially as consumers are stretched thin by inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. The company is also battling a slower housing market and higher mortgage rates. Ellison previously told CNBC he expects consumers to remain cautious through the end of the year.
